subject: general
question: Ghiyas ud-din Balban had set up a _______ department called 'Diwan-i-arz'.
solution:
The correct answer is __**military**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ghiyas ud-din Balban was a Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate from the Mamluk dynasty.
 
• He established the 'Diwan-i-arz' department to organize and manage the military affairs of the state.
 
• The 'Diwan-i-arz' was responsible for the recruitment, training, and payment of soldiers.
 
• This department played a crucial role in strengthening the military capabilities of the Delhi Sultanate under Balban's rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghiyas ud-din Balban**

 
 
• He was the ninth Sultan of the Mamluk dynasty of Delhi and ruled from 1266 to 1287.
 
• Balban was known for his strong centralized administration and efforts to maintain the integrity of the Sultanate against internal and external threats.
 
• He introduced various administrative reforms and was known for his strict enforcement of law and order.
 
• Balban's reign is often marked by his efforts to suppress the power of the nobility and consolidate the authority of the Sultan.
 
 
 
• **Diwan-i-arz**
 
 
• This was a military department established by Balban to oversee all aspects of military organization.
 
• The Diwan-i-arz was responsible for the recruitment of soldiers, their training, and their payment.
 
• It played a key role in maintaining the efficiency and readiness of the Sultanate's army.
 
• By creating this department, Balban ensured that his military forces were well-organized and capable of defending the Sultanate against any threats.
 
 
 
• **Mamluk Dynasty**
 
 
• The Mamluk dynasty was the first of the Delhi Sultanates and was established by Qutb-ud-din Aibak.
 
• The dynasty ruled the northern Indian subcontinent from 1206 to 1290.
 
• It is known for laying the foundation of Muslim rule in India and introducing Islamic culture and architecture.
 
• The Mamluks were originally slave soldiers who rose to power through military prowess and administrative skills.
